texts.preamble: Bansilal Manilal Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 19 June, 2018 Author: G.R.Udhwani Bench: G.R.Udhwani R/Cr.Ra/660/2017 Order
texts.facts: The petitioner was held guilty for misbranding of certain food articles.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner has invited the attention of this Court to Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan, Criminal Appeal No.214 of 2016 arising out of SLP (Criminal) No.2148 of 2013 decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. The learned counsel has further pointed out that by passing the further orders the order rendered in Nemi Chand (Supra) came to be clarified by order dated 17.03.2016, which reads as under: "Upon being mentioned by Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel for the appellant, the 8th line of page no.2 of order dated March 10, 2016, passed in the aforementioned criminal appeal, i.e., A "He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable. A is substituted by the following: A "He has, in this behalf, argued that under Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the maximum penalty is only fine for sub-standard food or misbranding. A (Nidhi Ahuja)." 2.1 The learned counsel submitted that in Nemi Chand (Supra) Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety And Standards Act, 2006 were retrospectively applied even to the pending cases. He submitted that in the instant case also except misbranding, no other charge was led against the petitioner, that the punishment for misbranding contemplated in Section 52 is fine only. The learned counsel therefore, urged to extend the benefit of the said provisions to the petitioner as well. He would submit that the petitioner would not press for the petition on other merits of the case. In Nemi Chand (Supra) benefit of Section 51 of the Act of 2006 came to be extended by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case arising under old law i.e. Act of 1954; the relevant observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court are thus: "It is not in dispute that the charge against the appellant was only of sub-standardization of goods. Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that though the appellant has some prima facie case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence which has been imposed by the courts below. He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable. He has drawn our attention to the judgment of this Court in 'T. Barai v. Henry Ah Hoe and Another' [1983 (1) SCC 177] wherein this Court held that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused persons, it can be applied even with respect to earlier cases as well which are pending in the Court." 4.
